criteria.notes: Three conjuncts: (a) succeeds against a disposable self-signed server, (b) library-level with 16's transport invoked directly, (c) integration test artifact. All three evidenced, and the load-bearing one was measured rather than read. Probe P5a: deleting customCaPem from the success case's GatewayHttpClient — leaving the real https server, the real cert and the real pinned dial untouched — turns the test RED with 'Error: self-signed certificate'. So the custom-CA path is genuinely load-bearing and TLS verification is genuinely on. Had it stayed green this would have been reported as a live security finding rather than a tick. Probe P5b: the address pinning does not weaken verification. A repo-wide grep for rejectUnauthorized finds exactly one hit, in an unrelated owner-gated @live attestation test; packages/gateway never disables verification, and http-transport.ts:86 keeps SNI servername set to the real hostname so the certificate is still validated against it. Scope note: the SSRF-guard preflight is satisfied with a fake non-loopback resolver answer while the actual dial is pinned to 127.0.0.1. That is the gateway's own reachability-probe pattern, documented in the test's header at :24-29, and it is what lets a real local server stand in for a self-hosted DC target; the guard itself is not bypassed, only fed a stand-in resolution.

criteria.notes: Four conjuncts: (a) rejects without allowBasicAuth: true, (b) accepts with it, (c) emits a non-blocking doctor finding, (d) unit AND integration test. All four evidenced, at three layers. Probe P6 (vacuity attack): deleting the assertBasicAuthPermitted(config) call at packages/connectors-jira/src/auth/jira-datacenter-auth.ts:90 reddens FOUR suites — jira-datacenter-auth, connection-doctor-datacenter, jira-datacenter-connection-registry and register-datacenter — 4 failed / 43 passed of 47 files. The guard is load-bearing at exactly the boundaries the criterion names. The non-blocking half is asserted by behaviour rather than by a finding's name: the allowed case returns ok: true AND basicAuthActive: true in the same result object, with a PAT-config control asserting basicAuthActive: false. The rejection half is proven pre-network by a call-count (expect(probeCalled).toBe(false)) and, at the registry, by expect(httpClientBuilt).toBe(false) — not by matching an error message. SCOPE NOTE so the "integration" conjunct is not over-read: the doctor's reachability probe is an injected seam, and no wire-level basic-auth round trip exists anywhere in the tree. The integration half is carried by the registry and routed-registration boundaries, where a disallowed config demonstrably never reaches buildHttpClient. That is exactly what roadmap/19 §In scope promises — "is rejected pre-network with canonical authentication (P02)" — so this reading needs no wording correction. Consumer-of-record note, not a defect: runJiraDatacenterConnectionDoctor has zero production callers today. roadmap/19 §Interfaces produced names its consumers as "this phase's own test suite directly and, later, 23's CLI-wiring work behind connection doctor <id>", so its current test-only reach is the declared design, not dead code.

criteria.notes: Four conjuncts: (a) 10.3 boots and passes a smoke test in CI, (b) 11.3 likewise, (c) reusable unmodified by 23's disposable-environment tooling, (d) CI artifact. (c) is evidenced; (a), (b) and (d) have no evidence and cannot acquire any in this pass. The channel is implemented and ready — .github/workflows/jira-datacenter-smoke.yml, a two-edition matrix over docker/jira-datacenter/{10.3,11.3}/docker-compose.yml driving docker/jira-datacenter/smoke-test.sh, requiring no secret by its own design. It has ZERO runs: gh run list --workflow=jira-datacenter-smoke.yml returns an empty list while the same query against ci.yml returns runs, so the emptiness is real and not a broken query. It is workflow_dispatch-only and no other workflow chains it. Consequence worth stating plainly: the image tags atlassian/jira-software:10.3 and :11.3 have never been validated by anything, not even for existence on Docker Hub. This pass is not authorised to dispatch the workflow or to boot a container locally, so the classification is EVIDENCE-NEEDS-CI and the box stays unticked. No defect record is filed: nothing is broken and nothing is missing from the tree — the gate is authorisation, not credentials and not code. Conjunct (c) is evidenced without booting anything, and pinned to a real run rather than to a file's existence: e2e/provisioning/test/jira-datacenter-wiring.test.ts parses both compose files at the exact paths phase 19 shipped and asserts the service name, the edition-pinned image tag, the healthcheck and the named volume that 23's harness drives, and it EXECUTED in the v1.5.0 release-gate run (job 91004033370, job-log line 626, 5 tests). Both the recipes and that test file are byte-unchanged between that run's commit 6b9dd7b and this record's HEAD, verified by git diff --stat. A green run conclusion alone would not have been that proof, which is why the job log was downloaded and the line quoted. Remedy: the owner or an authorised pass dispatches jira-datacenter-smoke; both matrix jobs must reach RUNNING; then cite both job logs and tick. e2e/provisioning/test/jira-datacenter-config.live.test.ts is @live and was not run.
